gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's own Elite 100 mini manual says a battery that has dropped to 0% should be recharged from AC, or from 'an input of over 100 W' if solar is used. The $531.05 Elite 100 mini + 100 W kit's panel is rated at exactly 100 W and makes less outdoors, so it cannot meet that line. The manual also lists solar input as '350 W Max., 12 V–60 V, 10 A Max.', a 2-minute surge of only 735–840 W, and a charging range of 32–104 °F, with error E086 'Charging temperature too low' below that.
standout_why: I opened the two pages ChatGPT cited most. powersized.com/solar-generator-kits covers solar-input caps, staying inside the station's voltage window, Voc adding up in series, MC4-to-XT60 adapters and a 75% planning figure. It says plainly that it does not cover charging temperature or MPPT limits, and it does not list the Elite 100 mini. stormwatts.com/articles/solar-generator-kits-compared-same-panel-watts quotes voltage and current windows for larger stations and says cold raises panel Voc. It does not list the Elite 100 mini, the mini's 10 A or 700 W limits, the 0%-recovery rule, or that LFP stations stop charging below 32 °F. I did not open the cited bluettipower.com/pages/solar-generator page. The voltage-window idea itself is already on both rival pages, so that part is not new. The new parts are the mini-specific rules and the cold-charging cutoff.
decides: The finding splits the two Elite 100 mini kits, our cheapest ~1 kWh kits under $700. The +200 W kit ($616.55 link, $649 store) gives the station twice the 100 W the manual asks for to recover from 0% by solar, and its 200 W stays under the 350 W / 10 A input limit. The +100 W kit ($531.05 link, $559 store) is a top-up kit: after a full drain in an outage, its own panel falls short of BLUETTI's 'over 100 W' rule, so the shopper needs wall power. One caveat: BLUETTI's kit page says the 200 W panel 'ships from 11.18', so the +200 W kit does not quite ship now. The mini's 700 W output and 735–840 W 2-minute surge (Power Lifting reaches 1,400 W for resistive loads only) make it a kit for small loads. A shopper planning on a fridge or 1,500 W+ appliances, as ChatGPT's answer framed it, belongs on a 1,800 W-class station. Under $700 those are the pre-order Elite 100 V2 or ALLPOWERS P1800 kits, or the rival EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic. Every LFP kit here stops charging below 32 °F (EcoFlow and BLUETTI both state 0 °C). The shopper should keep the station indoors and run the cable out to the panel; that is a usage note and does not change the pick.
candidates: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic + solar panel kit

findings.label: Solar recharge from 0% state of charge
findings.value: Manual text: 'Recommended to charge via an AC source; if using solar energy, ensure an input of over 100 W.' It also says to charge within 48 hours and to keep the unit at 5–35 °C (41–95 °F) for 6 hours before charging
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 mini Portable Power Station User Manual - Manuals+
findings.note: Under Maintenance and Care: 'If SoC drops to 0% during storage or startup'. This is a manuals.plus copy of BLUETTI's manual (published 2026-07-26). BLUETTI's own manual PDF (images.thdstatic.com/catalog/pdfImages/92/9272a86e-564f-44d2-861d-539422069954.pdf, titled 'Elite 100 mini ... A0 26.06.04') opened, but its text could not be pulled out. The 100 W kit's panel is rated at exactly 100 W, so it cannot give 'over 100 W' even at rated output.

findings.label: Solar (DC) input limit
findings.value: 350 W max, 12–60 V, 10 A max, XT60 port; manual says 'Do not use solar panels with an open circuit voltage higher than 60 V'
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 mini Portable Power Station User Manual - Manuals+
findings.note: Error E033 'PV overvoltage': keep the PV input within 12–60 V. BLUETTI's US product page says only 'up to 350W solar'; its Tech Specs tab was empty on 2026-11-17.

findings.label: AC output and surge
findings.value: 700 W max, 120 V; surge 735–840 W for 2 min, 840–1,050 W for 2 s, 1,050 W or more for 0.5 s; Power Lifting up to 1,400 W for pure resistive loads ('its actual output power is still 700 W')
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 mini Portable Power Station User Manual - Manuals+
findings.note: BLUETTI's US page agrees: 'Total output not to exceed 700W.'

findings.label: Charging temperature
findings.value: 0–40 °C (32–104 °F) to charge; −20–40 °C (−4–104 °F) to discharge; error E086 'Charging temperature too low'
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 mini Portable Power Station User Manual - Manuals+
findings.note: The manual says the battery is LiFePO4. Below 32 °F the station shows E086 and does not charge from solar or any other source.
